svg.title: The subtracted term is supported at the single contact x = 0. Its differentiated value on f(a) is exactly wab,cd, because g(l) j (0) = 1{j=l}. The resulting defect therefore vanishes on all first-order product jets. It vanishes on the order-zero and order-two jets by total inversion: the three remaining tensor indices give an odd sign whereas an even total test order gives an even sign. These finite contact subtractions preserve the pair and signed symmetries; reflection in a single axis kills a coefficient unless its four tensor indices occur in pairs. Thus the compensated conservation defect has no jets of total degree below three.
